rationale: ROUND 2, resubmitting on the same correlation after the round-1 REVISE (gating: reuse_agent). The gate said: three sibling matchers drifting apart is how this bug was created, so do not add a third hand-mirrored copy of the arms — unify, or say why not. ANSWER: unified. The pairing relation now lives ONCE, in datahelpers/slot_pairing.go (SlotIdentity + slotPairArmMatches + two direction functions, arms-outer so a weaker match on an early candidate never beats a stronger match on a later one), and all THREE askers call it: matchLockedRow and MergeLockedPageSlots become thin adapters over PairIncomingToStored, matchPreservedSectionIdx over PairStoredToIncoming. Equivalence for the two LIVE matchers is proven by their existing suites passing unchanged (6 matchLockedRow tests incl. identity/kebab/consumption; the TestMergeLockedPageSlots table) — matchLockedRow gains NO behaviour: its SlotIdentity views carry empty function/name (its loader does not join content_components), so the function arm is a structural no-op there, stated at the call site; widening it would be a change to make on its own evidence, not as a refactor side effect. Drift guards per bug_historian's fourth-matcher note: the core's header instructs new pairing sites to call it; wiring scans fail if any of the three re-inlines a private copy (datahelpers-side AST scan for the merge; actions-side selector scan for both matchers); the arm-priority pin was mutation-verified (loop-swap mutation: RED). GUARDIAN's consuming-set ask, answered with the census dated 2026-08-25: agents whose config references save_page_sections = council-gate, page-rerender, page-build-handler, site-work-orchestrator, tool-recreation-handler, pageflow-builder, fix-proposer, page-rebuild, required-fields-missing-handler, diagnose-agent (10 by config-text match); per the documented landmine, council-gate and fix-proposer match on PROMPT TEXT and carry no save step, so the real dispatching set is the other EIGHT — spanning both the build arm (diagnosed) and the rerender arm, whose incoming name space is slot names and whose behaviour is unchanged (slot-exact arm kept, field baseline = the 08-25 24-page rerender wave). GUARDIAN low (preservedSection hoist collision): verified — the package compiles and `grep -rn 'type preservedSection' platform/` returns exactly one declaration. DEBUG_HISTORIAN medium (shared-file commit hygiene): round 1 was verified with scripts/verify-head-builds.sh at a799579fd (OK, recorded in lane NOTES); round 2 will re-run it post-commit, and the commit is pathspec-explicit with `git status --porcelain` checked before and `git ls-tree` after. DEBUG_HISTORIAN low (post-deploy liveness): added to bugs_open/385 §9 and the lane handoff — build-provenance stamp + `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, PLUS the pod symbol probe `grep -aq matchPreservedSectionIdx /proc/1/exe` with a present-control (matchLockedRow, in the current binary) and an absent-control (a nonsense symbol), never a bare discovery grep. The original round-1 rationale (the 385 §5c diagnosis) stands unchanged below. --- bugs_open/385 §5c (cause established 2026-08-25, first-hand at every joint): on 2026-08-23 a build-arm rebuild of loancalculator.co.uk/tools/loan-vs-savings.html appended a byte-identical, component_id-NULL copy of the page's locked calculator beside the locked row, and the page then failed every re-render (self-perpetuating). The writer is save_page_sections_action.go's Layer 2 interactive-preservation block: its preload (build_status='deployed' AND interactive) selected the locked row — measured 2026-08-25, the ONLY locked row in the fleet satisfying that predicate, which is why nine sibling pages in the same wave were untouched — and its matcher judged 'is this stored tool already in the incoming set?' by EXACT SLOT-NAME STRING only. On the build arm the incoming names are the plan's component-function names, so the stored positional slot 'tool-2' read as 'dropped entirely' while the same component sat in the set as 'tool-loan-vs-savings' (resolved id and all), and the rescue arm appended the stored bytes with ComponentID '' (RFC_046 opt-in OFF). The lock guard then — working correctly — consumed the lock on the plan's entry and could not pair the appended one: the orphan. This is the THIRD of the save path's three 'already in the set' judgements; matchLockedRow was given an identity arm (182/189/204) and MergeLockedPageSlots was born mirroring it (LOCK-008); this one never was, and bugs_closed/189's own 'STILL OPEN' note predicted the survivor on 08-03. The fix gives the third matcher the same arms, from data its preload already fetches, extracted so tests execute the production decision. The armed population is 1 row fleet-wide (the victim's own locked row, still armed); the next build-arm rebuild of that page reproduces the damage until this lands.

plan.summary: ROUND 2 (unification, per the reuse gate): the save path's three 'is this section already represented?' matchers now decide through ONE shared relation in datahelpers/slot_pairing.go — arms: component identity, slot exact, slot kebab, component function/name, each guarded non-empty, arms-outer across candidates, consumption at the call site. matchLockedRow and MergeLockedPageSlots become adapters (byte-equivalent, proven by their existing suites unchanged); matchPreservedSectionIdx (round 1's fix, already at HEAD a799579fd) becomes the third adapter, keeping round 1's behaviour exactly. Wiring scans in both packages fail if any asker re-inlines a private copy; the arm-priority pin is mutation-verified.

edits.rationale: The single canonical pairing relation. Header carries the 385 history, the reuse-gate provenance (corr ece638fb), and the instruction that a NEW pairing site must call these rather than hand-rolling — bug_historian's fourth-matcher concern, addressed structurally.

The merge's pair() closure was a hand-mirrored copy of the arms (slot exact, slot kebab, function-or-name; no ids on the list side). It now builds SlotIdentity views and calls PairIncomingToStored with componentID '' — the identity arm stands down, the other arms are its old arms verbatim, so TestMergeLockedPageSlots passes unchanged. Doc comment rewritten: 'mirrors matchLockedRow' becomes 'IS the shared relation'.

Adapter over PairIncomingToStored. SlotIdentity views deliberately leave function/name EMPTY (loadActiveLockedRows does not join content_components), so the function arm is a structural no-op and behaviour is byte-equivalent — proven by the six existing matchLockedRow tests (identity beats naming, empty-identity refusal, single consumption, positional/kebab) passing unchanged. Widening this matcher to the function arm would mean joining cc in the loader — a behaviour change to make on its own evidence, stated in the doc comment.

Round 1's matcher (already at HEAD a799579fd) becomes the third adapter, over PairStoredToIncoming — behaviour identical to round 1 (stored ComponentName is not fetched by the Layer 2 preload, so that half of arm 4 stands down exactly as in round 1). All round-1 unit tests pass unchanged.

Pins only the core can carry: arm PRIORITY across candidates (mutation-verified — swapping the arm/candidate loops turns the relation per-candidate and the test goes RED), the non-empty guards, consumption on every arm, and the datahelpers-side wiring scan (MergeLockedPageSlots must call PairIncomingToStored; its behaviour table is an equivalence proof and stays green against a re-inlined copy — this is what goes red).

A reviewer should confirm the adapters add no arm: matchLockedRow's views carry empty function/name (arm 4 no-op); the merge passes componentID '' (arm 1 no-op). 2) Arm-3-vs-arm-4 priority is now explicit where the merge's old closure interleaved function-or-name in ONE pass — unchanged in effect because arm 4 IS that one combined pass, and the arm-priority pin covers the cross-candidate case the old code never distinguished. 3) The one behaviour delta remains round 1's, unchanged in round 2: Layer 2 judges representation by identity/function as well as slot name, so a stored deployed interactive row paired by identity takes keep/splice instead of re-append. 4) Shared-file hazard (debug_historian): commit is pathspec-explicit; verify-head-builds.sh re-run post-commit; the new datahelpers file and both test files are named on both add and commit. 5) Pre-existing and unrelated: findingcodes_scan_test fails at HEAD on WORK_ITEM_STATUS_OVERRIDE_REFUSED (the 396 lane's 2b46afbe6, already flagged in their bug file by another lane).
